manuscript.shared: Wilson stood where the road opened into the highland court. The sound of four hooves on stone was enough to make the arriving traveler look up. Neither man had won the previous week. One had gone into Mountain Lake; the other had climbed out of a vat of chili. Neither needed the other to remind him. Jake kept his hood low and his weapon clipped. “I didn't come to talk about last week.” Wilson shifted his weight. “Then give me something else to remember.” The road behind them remained open.

This time three pairs of eyes watched the same strip of water from one body. Phillip stopped at the edge. “Do you give everyone directions?” Bobby looked toward the sign rather than the snake. “Only when they ask.” A thin line of water moved across the mud. Neither mistook the other for a stranger.

Kevin looked at the visitor, then at the empty hands. “Nothing to sign?” Duckhook gave the ruins a measured glance. “Not today.” The answer hung between them longer than the greeting. manuscript.shared: Jordan had learned the difference between promising a delivery and bringing one home. At the yard, he checked the straps before he greeted Brandon. The smell of cooking drifted across the open space; a week earlier Brandon had thrown a ball into a target and Jordan had stopped a truck before it followed two lost kegs. “You're early,” Jordan said. manuscript.shared: Ben stopped before he entered. The last road he had taken had promised a crossing and given him high water instead. This time he wanted to see the door before he trusted the weather. Manning waited within sight of it, with the wind making conversation difficult. “You can come in,” he said. Ben looked at the sky. “That's not the part I'm worried about.” They had both arrived at the same record; neither had been promised a place among the seven. The open doorway mattered more than a distant island.
